# Review

## Summary
The G25 host-only quiescence sweep enumerates the full executor inventory (actions ∪ admissions, including released, settled, and missing-hold rows), verifies journaled exit for every action generation plus the current worker generation before any Docker access, and stops only explicitly registered, exactly-journaled contained invocations under an explicit `stop_contained` mode with re-validated synchronous grants. Released admissions are opened strictly in `read_only` mode and can never be stopped (`CONTAINED_INSPECTION_CANNOT_STOP` before any daemon call). No ledger mutation, release, replay, or container recreation is possible: both stores are constructed with throwing verifiers, and the executor's `authorize('start')` unconditionally throws.

Guards are captured synchronously (structured-cloned request/registrations/options, captured grant references), and every async boundary re-runs `guard()` — comparing inventory digest and re-canonicalized worker exit observations — plus `recheck` in the reopen path re-validates admission digest and journal binding before each read/stop. Drift tests (release, revision, grant revocation, late worker-journal event, substituted bindings/manifests) confirm rejection before subsequent physical operations. Reports keep `recoveryAuthorized: false`, `workerDescendantsStatus`/`workspaceStatus: 'unproven'`, and only set `allInventoriedExecutorsStopped` when every worker and every inventoried executor is proven stopped; unknown states carry explicit reasons (`WORKER_EXIT_UNPROVEN`, `ADMISSION_MISSING`, `EXECUTOR_VERIFIER_UNAVAILABLE`, `CONTAINED_STOP_UNPROVEN`). Tests exercise real worker exit via the actual runtime, two independent contained invocations with distinct bound receipts, read-only release inspection, lost/uncertain receipts without repeated deletion, and cross-boundary state drift; 52 tests pass.

## Notes
- Info: worker generations are derived from action/admission inventory plus the current run generation; a hypothetical intermediate lease generation with zero actions and zero admissions would not be exit-verified. Such a generation has no inventoried executors to clean, and descendant state is already reported `unproven`, so this is not blocking.

# Review

The sweep enumerates the complete inventory (actions union admissions, including released/settled/missing-hold rows) and verifies journaled exit for every action generation plus the current worker before any Docker call. Only explicitly registered, exactly-journaled contained invocations are reopened; released admissions open read_only and can never stop; no recreation, ledger mutation, or release is reachable (throwing recovery verifiers, start always rejected). Captured clones/references plus guard()/recheck re-validation reject grant, inventory, and worker-journal drift across every async boundary, before subsequent physical operations. Claims stay diagnostic-only: recoveryAuthorized false, workspace/worker-descendant status unproven, unknown states explicit. Tests cover real worker exit, independent contained identities with distinct receipts, readonly release, uncertain/lost receipts without repeated deletion, and drift; 52 pass.

judgments.summary: Inventory is actions union admissions; every entry (held, released, settled, missing-admission) is observed with explicit reasons, and worker exit is verified for all entry generations plus the current run generation before any executor handling. Tests confirm released and missing-admission rows are never omitted or inferred stopped.

Stops require explicit stop_contained mode, a held (non-released) admission, an exact trusted registration matching ledger/journal binding, and current synchronous grants re-checked per operation. Recovery stores use throwing verifiers and executor start is unconditionally rejected, so no recreation, replay, ledger mutation, or admission release occurs; tests assert unchanged action state, held admission, and single DELETE.

Request, registrations, and contained options are cloned and grants captured synchronously; guard() recompares inventory digest and re-canonicalized worker observations at every boundary and inside wrapped authorize callbacks, while reopen's recheck re-validates admission digest and journal bytes before each read/stop. Drift tests (release, revision, grant revocation, late worker event) reject before further daemon operations.

Report hardcodes recoveryAuthorized false and workspaceStatus/workerDescendantsStatus unproven; allInventoriedExecutorsStopped requires all workers stopped AND all executor observations stopped. Opaque, unregistered, missing-admission, and unverified states remain explicitly unproven with reasons; no global quiescence or G15 authority is inferred.

52 tests pass, including real runtime worker exit observation, two distinct contained invocations with independently bound receipts, read_only inspection of released admissions with stop rejection, missing/lost stop receipts staying unknown without repeated deletion, and cross-async-boundary drift (release, revision, grant, worker journal, substituted manifests) rejected before Docker calls.
